question: Which article empowers the Supreme Court to exercise the jurisdiction and powers of the federal court under any pre-constitution law?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 135**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• **Article 135** of the Indian Constitution empowers the Supreme Court to exercise the jurisdiction and powers of a federal court under any pre-constitution law in certain cases.
 
• This provision ensures that the Supreme Court retains jurisdiction in matters where powers were exercised by the Federal Court of India before the Constitution came into effect.
 
• The Federal Court of India, established under the **Government of India Act, 1935**, was a precursor to the Supreme Court of India.
 
• Article 135 allows the Supreme Court to hear cases related to pre-constitutional laws until they are repealed or amended by Parliament.
 
• This article plays a crucial role in ensuring continuity and stability in India’s legal framework during the transition from colonial to independent governance.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Federal Court of India (1937-1950):**

 
 
• It was established under the Government of India Act, 1935, to resolve disputes between provinces and hear appeals against decisions of the High Courts.
 
• The Federal Court was replaced by the Supreme Court of India upon the adoption of the Constitution in 1950.
 
 
 
• **Government of India Act, 1935:**
 
 
• It was a significant constitutional reform by the British Parliament that served as a blueprint for India’s federal structure.
 
• It introduced provincial autonomy and a federal court system in British India.
 
 
 
• **Jurisdiction of the Supreme Court:**
 
 
• The Supreme Court has original, appellate, and advisory jurisdiction under Articles 131-136 and Article 143 of the Constitution.
 
• Article 135 complements these powers by extending the Court’s jurisdiction over pre-constitutional legal matters.
 
 
 
• **Continuity of Legal Framework:**
 
 
• Article 372 of the Constitution also ensures that laws in force before the adoption of the Constitution continue unless repealed or amended.
 
• In combination with Article 135, this ensures seamless legal continuity during India’s transition to constitutional democracy.
